title: Changing the structure and finding harmony
meaning: You can rebuild shared work when decisiveness about abandoning an old scheme allows time for fresh coordination.
text: When a familiar arrangement no longer withstands examination, a decisive revision may be needed. The Tower in the physical position of Manipura describes the action: dismantling an unsound scheme and ceasing to maintain the appearance of order. The Tower in energy identifies the motive, removing a foundation that no longer offers reliable support. Temperance in emotions lets you seek coordination between what remains and another way of working. The two Towers distinguish an act from its purpose. Emotional integration does not make the break painless or automatically beneficial.

Imagine that a shared folder system has thoroughly confused your documents. You stop adding files under the old rule and begin sorting what accumulated. **Fresh coordination needs space after a decisive rejection of the old.** Clear names can remain while you redistribute the rest. Everything need not be restored in one evening for you to feel that actions are beginning to fit together again.

The difficulty appears if you dismantle the earlier scheme quickly and expect new coordination just as immediately. Every remaining confusion then provokes irritation and another revision. Seeking harmony, you introduce increasingly abrupt changes. Temperance needs room to combine real differences. It supports shared will when an interim arrangement can be tried in practice before you decide once again that everything must be rebuilt.
